title: Step‑by‑Step Garlic‑Infused Butter for Holiday Roast Turkey
meta_description: Learn how to make garlic‑infused butter for a juicy holiday roast turkey using a sturdy garlic press—simple steps, bold flavor, perfect festive results.
html:
When you’re prepping a holiday roast turkey, the secret to moist meat and a mouth‑watering crust often lies in the butter you baste with. A garlic‑infused butter made with a reliable garlic press delivers intense flavor without the hassle of mincing cloves by hand. Below is a step‑by‑step guide that shows you exactly how to create a silky garlic press butter holiday turkey spread that will become a staple in your holiday kitchen.

Why Garlic‑Press Butter Beats Traditional Garlic Paste

Using a garlic press eliminates the uneven texture you get from a knife‑chopped paste. The press forces every clove through a fine mesh, releasing essential oils and creating a uniform, aromatic paste that blends seamlessly into softened butter. This method also saves time—especially valuable when you’re juggling multiple dishes on oven day.

Gather Your Ingredients and Tools

Before you start, assemble the following items. Having everything at hand keeps you focused on the turkey rather than hunting for missing components.

  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
  • 6–8 garlic cloves (adjust to taste)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, finely chopped
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  • Salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
  • Garlic Press (sturdy stainless and silicone model)
  • Small mixing bowl, rubber spatula, and a piece of parchment paper

Step 1: Press the Garlic

Place the peeled garlic cloves into the chamber of your Garlic Press. Squeeze firmly—your stainless‑steel mechanism will crush the cloves and push the minced garlic through the silicone head, delivering a smooth, almost paste‑like consistency. The press also collects the skins, making cleanup a breeze. You’ll end up with roughly 2 tablespoons of freshly pressed garlic, which is far more aromatic than pre‑minced jarred garlic.

Step 2: Combine Butter and Aromatics

In a medium bowl, add the softened butter. Using a rubber spatula, fold in the pressed garlic, chopped rosemary, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix until the green specks are evenly distributed and the butter takes on a creamy, glossy appearance. If the butter feels too stiff, let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes; it should spread easily without melting.

Step 3: Prepare the Turkey for Butter Application

Pat your turkey dry with paper towels—moisture hinders browning. Gently loosen the skin over the breast and thighs by sliding your hand under the skin, being careful not to tear it. This creates a pocket for the butter to melt into, ensuring the meat stays juicy beneath the crisp skin.

Step 4: Apply the Garlic‑Infused Butter

Take a generous spoonful of the garlic‑press butter and slide it under the loosened skin, spreading it across the meat. Then rub the remaining butter over the exterior of the turkey, covering the legs, wings, and back. The butter will melt during roasting, baste the meat, and create a golden, fragrant crust.

Step 5: Roast and Baste

Preheat your oven to 325°F (163°C). Place the turkey on a rack in a roasting pan and tent the breast loosely with foil to protect it from over‑browning. Roast according to your turkey’s weight—generally 13‑15 minutes per pound—basting every 30 minutes with pan juices. In the final 30 minutes, remove the foil to let the skin turn deep amber. The garlic‑press butter will have infused the meat with a mellow, caramelized garlic flavor while keeping the skin delightfully crisp.

Finishing Touches and Storage

After the turkey reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) in the thickest thigh, let it rest for at least 20 minutes before carving. This rest period allows the butter to redistribute, locking in moisture. Any leftover garlic‑infused butter can be rolled into a log on parchment, chilled, and sliced for future use on steaks, roasted vegetables, or even warm bread.

FAQ

Can I use a regular garlic press if it’s not stainless steel?

Yes, any sturdy press will work, but stainless steel resists corrosion and lasts longer, especially when dealing with acidic ingredients like lemon zest.

Do I need to melt the butter before mixing it with the garlic?

No. Softened butter at room temperature blends best with pressed garlic, preserving the airy texture that spreads evenly over the turkey.

Is it okay to add other herbs besides rosemary?

Absolutely. Thyme, sage, or even a pinch of smoked paprika can complement the garlic‑press butter and give your holiday turkey a unique twist.
